title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Diabetes Self-Management Education by Community Health Workers
target_population: Adults with Type 2 diabetes in Medicaid populations, particularly Hispanic/Latino and African American communities
implementation_guidance: Implement 6-session culturally tailored diabetes education program using CFIR framework. Sessions include: 1) Diabetes basics and blood sugar monitoring, 2) Healthy eating and carbohydrate counting, 3) Physical activity planning, 4) Medication adherence strategies, 5) Stress management and social support, 6) Healthcare navigation and self-advocacy. Each session 90 minutes, delivered in community settings.
expected_outcomes: Significant reduction in HbA1c levels (mean decrease 0.8-1.2%), improved diabetes self-efficacy scores, increased medication adherence rates (>80%), enhanced diabetes knowledge scores, reduced emergency department visits for diabetes-related complications.
evidence_base: Shah et al. (2013). The Role of Community Health Workers in Diabetes: Update on Current Literature. Current Diabetes Reports, 13(2), 163-171.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Diabetes Prevention by Community Health Workers
target_population: Adults with prediabetes in high-risk communities, particularly Hispanic/Latino and African American populations
implementation_guidance: Deliver 16-session lifestyle intervention program based on Diabetes Prevention Program. Include: nutrition education, physical activity promotion, weight management strategies, stress reduction techniques, and social support building. Sessions delivered over 6 months in community settings.
expected_outcomes: 5-7% weight loss, 150+ minutes weekly physical activity, reduced progression to Type 2 diabetes by 58%, improved dietary habits, enhanced self-efficacy for lifestyle changes.
evidence_base: Nelson et al. (2017). Randomized Controlled Trial of a Community Health Worker Self-Management Support Intervention Among Low-Income Adults With Diabetes. Preventing Chronic Disease, 14, E15.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Hypertension Medication Adherence by Care Coordinators
target_population: Adults with hypertension in Medicaid populations with medication adherence challenges
implementation_guidance: Implement multifactorial intervention including: patient education sessions, medication adherence monitoring, care coordination with providers, home blood pressure monitoring support, and lifestyle counseling. Monthly contacts for 12 months using CFIR framework.
expected_outcomes: Improved medication adherence rates (>80%), significant reduction in systolic blood pressure (10-15 mmHg), decreased cardiovascular events, enhanced patient self-management skills.
evidence_base: Pladevall et al. (2010). Multicenter Cluster-Randomized Trial of a Multifactorial Intervention to Improve Antihypertensive Medication Adherence and Blood Pressure Control. Circulation, 122(12), 1183-1191.

title: Evidence-Based Protocol for Depression Screening and Referral by Behavioral Health Care Managers
target_population: Adults in primary care settings, particularly those with chronic conditions and social determinants of health challenges
implementation_guidance: Implement systematic depression screening using PHQ-9, provide brief interventions for mild-moderate depression, coordinate referrals for specialty care, and deliver care management services. Follow collaborative care model with monthly assessments.
expected_outcomes: Increased depression screening rates (>90%), improved depression outcomes (50% reduction in PHQ-9 scores), enhanced access to mental health services, reduced healthcare utilization.
evidence_base: Gilbody et al. (2006). Collaborative care for depression: a cumulative meta-analysis and review of longer-term outcomes. Archives of Internal Medicine, 166(21), 2314-2321.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Hypertension Management by Community Health Workers
target_population: Adults with uncontrolled hypertension in underserved communities
implementation_guidance: Deliver comprehensive hypertension management program including: blood pressure monitoring training, medication adherence support, lifestyle modification counseling, healthcare navigation assistance, and social support facilitation. Home visits and community-based sessions over 12 months.
expected_outcomes: Significant blood pressure reduction (systolic BP decrease 8-12 mmHg), improved medication adherence, increased healthcare engagement, enhanced self-management behaviors.
evidence_base: Mbuthia et al. (2022). Approaches and outcomes of community health worker interventions for hypertension management and control in low-income and middle-income countries. BMJ Open, 12(4), e053455.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Diabetes Medication Management by Clinical Pharmacists
target_population: Adults with Type 2 diabetes and medication adherence challenges in primary care settings
implementation_guidance: Provide comprehensive medication therapy management including: medication reconciliation, adherence counseling, side effect management, drug interaction screening, and collaborative care with primary care providers. Monthly follow-up visits for 6 months.
expected_outcomes: Improved medication adherence (>85%), reduced HbA1c levels (0.5-1.0% decrease), decreased medication-related problems, enhanced patient satisfaction with diabetes care.
evidence_base: Sharp et al. (2018). Community health workers supporting clinical pharmacists in diabetes management: a randomized controlled trial. Pharmacotherapy, 38(6), 651-662.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Asthma Action Plan Education by Clinical Pharmacists
target_population: Children and adults with asthma in underserved communities, particularly those with frequent exacerbations
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive asthma education program including: inhaler technique training, asthma action plan development, trigger identification and avoidance, medication adherence counseling, and emergency management education. Individual and group sessions over 3 months.
expected_outcomes: Improved inhaler technique (>90% correct use), reduced asthma exacerbations (40-60% decrease), decreased emergency department visits, enhanced asthma control scores, improved quality of life measures.
evidence_base: Gibson et al. (2002). Self-management education and regular practitioner review for adults with asthma. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, (3), CD001117.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for COPD Self-Management by Clinical Pharmacists
target_population: Adults with moderate to severe COPD in primary care and community settings
implementation_guidance: Deliver 6-step comprehensive COPD self-management program including: pathophysiology education, inhaler technique optimization, exacerbation action plan development, pulmonary rehabilitation referral, smoking cessation support, and vaccination coordination. Monthly sessions for 6 months.
expected_outcomes: 25-40% reduction in COPD exacerbations, improved inhaler technique, enhanced quality of life scores, reduced hospitalizations, improved medication adherence, increased smoking cessation rates.
evidence_base: Zwerink et al. (2014). Self management for patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, (3), CD002990.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Heart Failure Self-Care Education by Nurse Care Managers
target_population: Adults with heart failure in community and primary care settings, particularly those with frequent hospitalizations
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive heart failure self-care program including: symptom monitoring education, medication management, dietary sodium restriction, fluid management, exercise planning, and early recognition of decompensation. Weekly contacts for first month, then monthly for 6 months.
expected_outcomes: 30-50% reduction in heart failure hospitalizations, improved self-care behaviors, enhanced quality of life scores, increased medication adherence, reduced healthcare costs.
evidence_base: McAlister et al. (2004). Multidisciplinary strategies for the management of heart failure patients at high risk for admission: a systematic review of randomized trials. Journal of the American College of Cardiology, 44(4), 810-819.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for CKD Education and Monitoring by Clinical Pharmacists
target_population: Adults with stages 3-4 chronic kidney disease in primary care settings
implementation_guidance: Provide comprehensive CKD management including: disease progression education, medication dosing adjustments, blood pressure optimization, cardiovascular risk reduction, bone and mineral disorder management, and preparation for renal replacement therapy. Quarterly visits for 12 months.
expected_outcomes: Slowed CKD progression, improved blood pressure control, reduced cardiovascular events, enhanced patient knowledge of CKD, improved medication adherence, delayed need for dialysis.
evidence_base: Salgado et al. (2012). Pharmacist-provided chronic kidney disease management in primary care: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Pharmacotherapy, 32(6), 499-514.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Prenatal Care Coordination by Doulas
target_population: Pregnant women in Medicaid populations, particularly those with high-risk pregnancies and social vulnerabilities
implementation_guidance: Provide comprehensive prenatal support including: childbirth education, emotional support, advocacy during medical appointments, resource navigation, breastfeeding support, and postpartum care coordination. Continuous support from 20 weeks gestation through 6 weeks postpartum.
expected_outcomes: Reduced preterm birth rates (15-25% decrease), improved birth outcomes, increased breastfeeding initiation and duration, enhanced maternal satisfaction with care, reduced postpartum depression rates.
evidence_base: Hodnett et al. (2013). Continuous support for women during childbirth. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, (7), CD003766.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Substance Use Screening and Brief Intervention by Peer Recovery Specialists
target_population: Adults with substance use disorders in healthcare and community settings, particularly those in early recovery
implementation_guidance: Implement SBIRT (Screening, Brief Intervention, and Referral to Treatment) protocol including: validated screening tools, motivational interviewing techniques, harm reduction counseling, treatment referral coordination, and ongoing recovery support. Weekly contacts for first month, then bi-weekly for 6 months.
expected_outcomes: Increased treatment engagement (60-80% completion rates), reduced substance use frequency and quantity, improved recovery self-efficacy, decreased criminal justice involvement, enhanced social support networks.
evidence_base: Bernstein et al. (2005). Brief motivational intervention at a clinic visit reduces cocaine and heroin use. Drug and Alcohol Dependence, 77(1), 49-59.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Care Transitions by Nurse Care Managers
target_population: High-risk patients transitioning from hospital to home, particularly elderly with multiple chronic conditions
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive care transitions intervention including: medication reconciliation, discharge planning, home visit within 48 hours, patient/caregiver education, primary care follow-up coordination, and 30-day telephone support. Follow Coleman Care Transitions Model.
expected_outcomes: 30-40% reduction in 30-day readmissions, improved medication adherence, enhanced patient activation scores, reduced emergency department visits, improved patient satisfaction with care transitions.
evidence_base: Coleman et al. (2006). The care transitions intervention: results of a randomized controlled trial. Archives of Internal Medicine, 166(17), 1822-1828.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Social Determinants Screening and Intervention by Social Workers
target_population: Vulnerable populations in healthcare settings with housing, food, transportation, and financial insecurity
implementation_guidance: Conduct systematic screening for social determinants of health using validated tools, provide resource navigation and advocacy, coordinate with community-based organizations, and deliver case management services. Monthly contacts for 6 months with intensive support for high-need cases.
expected_outcomes: Improved access to social services (>80% successful referrals), reduced food insecurity, enhanced housing stability, increased healthcare utilization for preventive services, improved health outcomes.
evidence_base: Gottlieb et al. (2017). A systematic review of interventions on patients' social and economic needs. American Journal of Preventive Medicine, 53(5), 719-729.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Pediatric Asthma Management by Community Health Workers
target_population: Children with asthma in low-income families, particularly in urban environments with environmental triggers
implementation_guidance: Deliver comprehensive pediatric asthma management program including: family education on asthma triggers, home environmental assessment and remediation, inhaler technique training for children and caregivers, school coordination, and emergency action plan development. Home visits and community sessions over 12 months.
expected_outcomes: 40-60% reduction in asthma exacerbations, decreased emergency department visits, improved school attendance, enhanced caregiver confidence in asthma management, reduced environmental triggers in home.
evidence_base: Parker et al. (2008). Neighborhood-based asthma intervention for children. New England Journal of Medicine, 358(14), 1457-1466.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Medication Reconciliation by Clinical Pharmacists
target_population: Patients with polypharmacy in care transition settings, particularly elderly and chronically ill populations
implementation_guidance: Conduct comprehensive medication reconciliation including: medication history verification, identification of discrepancies, resolution of drug therapy problems, patient/caregiver education, and communication with healthcare providers. Performed at all care transitions with 30-day follow-up.
expected_outcomes: 50-70% reduction in medication errors, decreased adverse drug events, improved medication adherence, reduced healthcare utilization, enhanced patient safety outcomes.
evidence_base: Kwan et al. (2013). Medication reconciliation during transitions of care as a patient safety strategy: a systematic review. Annals of Internal Medicine, 158(5 Pt 2), 397-403.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Chronic Disease Self-Management by Community Health Workers
target_population: Adults with multiple chronic conditions in underserved communities, particularly racial/ethnic minorities
implementation_guidance: Implement Stanford Chronic Disease Self-Management Program including: goal setting and action planning, problem-solving techniques, symptom management, medication adherence support, communication with healthcare providers, and peer support facilitation. 6-week group sessions with ongoing support.
expected_outcomes: Improved self-efficacy for managing chronic conditions, enhanced quality of life scores, reduced healthcare utilization, improved medication adherence, increased physical activity levels.
evidence_base: Lorig et al. (2001). Chronic disease self-management program: 2-year health status and health care utilization outcomes. Medical Care, 39(11), 1217-1223.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Transitions of Care for High-Risk Patients by Social Workers
target_population: High-risk patients with complex social needs transitioning between care settings
implementation_guidance: Provide comprehensive discharge planning and care coordination including: social determinants assessment, resource identification and linkage, insurance and benefits navigation, transportation coordination, and post-discharge follow-up. Intensive case management for 30 days post-discharge.
expected_outcomes: Reduced 30-day readmission rates, improved access to community resources, enhanced patient satisfaction with discharge process, increased primary care follow-up rates, reduced emergency department utilization.
evidence_base: Jack et al. (2009). A reengineered hospital discharge program to decrease rehospitalization: a randomized trial. Annals of Internal Medicine, 150(3), 178-187.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Mental Health Screening in Primary Care by Behavioral Health Care Managers
target_population: Adults in primary care settings with risk factors for depression and anxiety disorders
implementation_guidance: Implement systematic mental health screening using validated tools (PHQ-9, GAD-7), provide brief interventions, coordinate integrated behavioral health services, and deliver care management. Follow collaborative care model with psychiatric consultation.
expected_outcomes: Increased detection of mental health conditions (>85% screening rate), improved depression and anxiety outcomes, enhanced access to behavioral health services, reduced stigma associated with mental health treatment.
evidence_base: Archer et al. (2012). Collaborative care for depression and anxiety problems. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, (10), CD006525.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Substance Use Prevention by Peer Recovery Specialists
target_population: Adolescents and young adults at risk for substance use disorders in community settings
implementation_guidance: Deliver evidence-based prevention programming including: risk and protective factor education, life skills training, peer support groups, family engagement activities, and community mobilization efforts. School and community-based sessions over academic year.
expected_outcomes: Reduced initiation of substance use, delayed age of first use, improved protective factors (self-esteem, social skills), enhanced family communication, increased community awareness of substance use issues.
evidence_base: Spoth et al. (2008). The PROSPER community-university partnership model for public education systems: a first look at effectiveness. American Journal of Preventive Medicine, 35(6), 570-579.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Medication Management in Polypharmacy by Clinical Pharmacists
target_population: Elderly adults with polypharmacy (5+ medications) in primary care and community settings
implementation_guidance: Conduct comprehensive medication reviews including: medication appropriateness assessment, drug interaction screening, adherence evaluation, cost optimization, and patient education. Collaborative care with primary care providers with quarterly reviews.
expected_outcomes: Reduced potentially inappropriate medications, decreased adverse drug events, improved medication adherence, reduced healthcare costs, enhanced patient knowledge of medications.
evidence_base: Jokanovic et al. (2017). Pharmacist-led medication review in community settings: An overview of systematic reviews. Research in Social and Administrative Pharmacy, 13(4), 661-685.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Maternal Depression Screening by Doulas
target_population: Pregnant and postpartum women in Medicaid populations with risk factors for perinatal depression
implementation_guidance: Implement systematic perinatal depression screening using EPDS, provide emotional support and counseling, coordinate referrals to mental health services, and deliver postpartum support. Screening at multiple time points from pregnancy through 12 months postpartum.
expected_outcomes: Increased detection of perinatal depression (>90% screening rate), improved maternal mental health outcomes, enhanced mother-infant bonding, reduced postpartum depression severity, increased treatment engagement.
evidence_base: O'Connor et al. (2016). Primary care screening for and treatment of depression in pregnant and postpartum women: evidence report and systematic review. JAMA, 315(4), 388-406.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Social Isolation Intervention by Social Workers
target_population: Elderly adults experiencing social isolation and loneliness in community settings
implementation_guidance: Deliver multi-component social isolation intervention including: social skills training, community engagement activities, volunteer matching, technology training for virtual connections, and group-based activities. Individual and group sessions over 6 months.
expected_outcomes: Reduced social isolation scores, improved mental health outcomes, enhanced social network size and quality, increased community engagement, improved overall well-being and life satisfaction.
evidence_base: Masi et al. (2011). A meta-analysis of interventions to reduce loneliness. Personality and Social Psychology Review, 15(3), 219-266.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Care Coordination for Complex Patients by Care Coordinators
target_population: Adults with multiple chronic conditions and frequent healthcare utilization
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive care coordination including: care plan development, provider communication, appointment scheduling and transportation, medication management support, and patient advocacy. Intensive case management with weekly contacts initially, then monthly maintenance.
expected_outcomes: Reduced healthcare utilization, improved care coordination scores, enhanced patient satisfaction, decreased emergency department visits, improved medication adherence, better chronic disease management.
evidence_base: Peikes et al. (2009). Effects of care coordination on hospitalization, quality of care, and health care expenditures among Medicare beneficiaries. JAMA, 301(6), 603-618.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Pediatric Obesity Prevention by Community Health Workers
target_population: Children and families in low-income communities at risk for childhood obesity
implementation_guidance: Deliver family-based obesity prevention program including: nutrition education, physical activity promotion, screen time reduction, family meal planning, grocery store tours, and cooking classes. Home visits and community sessions over 12 months.
expected_outcomes: Reduced BMI percentiles in children, improved dietary habits, increased physical activity levels, enhanced family nutrition knowledge, reduced screen time, improved family eating behaviors.
evidence_base: Slusser et al. (2012). Improving overweight among at-risk minority youth: results of a pilot intervention in after-school programs. Journal of Health Care for the Poor and Underserved, 23(4), 1472-1486.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Tobacco Cessation by Behavioral Health Care Managers
target_population: Adults with tobacco use disorder in healthcare and community settings
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive tobacco cessation program including: motivational interviewing, nicotine replacement therapy coordination, behavioral counseling, relapse prevention planning, and ongoing support. Individual and group sessions over 6 months with 12-month follow-up.
expected_outcomes: Increased tobacco cessation rates (25-35% at 6 months), reduced tobacco use frequency, improved respiratory health outcomes, enhanced motivation for quitting, reduced healthcare costs.
evidence_base: Stead et al. (2017). Combined pharmacotherapy and behavioural interventions for smoking cessation. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, (3), CD008286.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Diabetes Foot Care by Community Health Workers
target_population: Adults with diabetes at risk for foot complications in underserved communities
implementation_guidance: Deliver comprehensive diabetic foot care education including: daily foot inspection techniques, proper foot hygiene, appropriate footwear selection, nail care, wound prevention, and early recognition of complications. Monthly group sessions with individual assessments.
expected_outcomes: Reduced diabetic foot ulcers (40-60% decrease), decreased lower extremity amputations, improved foot care behaviors, enhanced patient knowledge of foot care, increased healthcare seeking for foot problems.
evidence_base: Dorresteijn et al. (2014). Patient education for preventing diabetic foot ulceration. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, (12), CD001488.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Immunization Outreach by Community Health Workers
target_population: Children in underserved communities with incomplete immunization schedules
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive immunization outreach program including: immunization status assessment, vaccine education for parents, appointment scheduling assistance, transportation support, and follow-up for missed appointments. Community-based outreach with home visits as needed.
expected_outcomes: Increased immunization completion rates (>90% up-to-date status), reduced vaccine-preventable disease incidence, improved parental vaccine confidence, enhanced healthcare engagement, reduced health disparities.
evidence_base: Jacobson Vann et al. (2018). Patient reminder and recall systems to improve immunization rates. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, (1), CD003941.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Chronic Pain Management by Nurse Care Managers
target_population: Adults with chronic pain conditions in primary care settings
implementation_guidance: Deliver comprehensive chronic pain management program including: pain assessment and monitoring, non-pharmacological pain management techniques, medication optimization, functional goal setting, and psychological support. Monthly visits with interdisciplinary team coordination.
expected_outcomes: Improved pain management scores, enhanced functional status, reduced opioid dependence, improved quality of life measures, increased use of non-pharmacological pain management strategies.
evidence_base: Kroenke et al. (2009). Optimized antidepressant therapy and pain self-management in primary care patients with depression and musculoskeletal pain. JAMA, 301(20), 2099-2110.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Breast Cancer Screening by Community Health Workers
target_population: Women in underserved communities with barriers to breast cancer screening
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive breast cancer screening program including: education about screening guidelines, navigation assistance for mammography appointments, transportation coordination, results follow-up, and emotional support. Culturally tailored approach with peer support.
expected_outcomes: Increased mammography screening rates (>80% adherence to guidelines), reduced time to diagnostic follow-up, improved breast cancer knowledge, enhanced healthcare engagement, reduced breast cancer mortality.
evidence_base: Wells et al. (2011). Community health workers and breast cancer screening: a systematic review. Journal of the American Board of Family Medicine, 24(5), 589-597.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Colorectal Cancer Screening by Care Coordinators
target_population: Adults aged 50-75 in primary care settings with incomplete colorectal cancer screening
implementation_guidance: Deliver comprehensive colorectal cancer screening program including: screening option education, shared decision-making support, appointment scheduling, preparation instructions, results communication, and follow-up coordination. Patient navigation throughout screening process.
expected_outcomes: Increased colorectal cancer screening rates (>75% completion), improved screening method completion, reduced time to follow-up for abnormal results, enhanced patient satisfaction with screening process.
evidence_base: Percac-Lima et al. (2009). The longitudinal impact of patient navigation on equity in colorectal cancer screening in a large primary care network. Cancer, 115(19), 4669-4676.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Cervical Cancer Screening by Community Health Workers
target_population: Women in underserved communities with barriers to cervical cancer screening
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive cervical cancer screening program including: HPV and Pap test education, appointment scheduling assistance, transportation coordination, results follow-up, and emotional support. Culturally appropriate education and peer support.
expected_outcomes: Increased cervical cancer screening rates (>85% adherence to guidelines), improved follow-up for abnormal results, enhanced HPV vaccination rates, reduced cervical cancer incidence, improved women's health knowledge.
evidence_base: Lewin et al. (2010). Lay health workers in primary and community health care for maternal and child health and the management of infectious diseases. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, (3), CD004015.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for HIV Prevention by Peer Recovery Specialists
target_population: Adults at high risk for HIV infection, particularly those with substance use disorders
implementation_guidance: Deliver comprehensive HIV prevention program including: risk assessment, HIV testing coordination, pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) education, harm reduction counseling, and linkage to HIV care services. Peer-based approach with ongoing support.
expected_outcomes: Increased HIV testing rates, improved PrEP uptake and adherence, reduced high-risk behaviors, enhanced linkage to HIV care, decreased HIV transmission rates in high-risk populations.
evidence_base: Medley et al. (2009). Effectiveness of peer education interventions for HIV prevention in developing countries: a systematic review and meta-analysis. AIDS Education and Prevention, 21(3), 181-206.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Hepatitis C Screening and Treatment by Clinical Pharmacists
target_population: Adults at risk for hepatitis C infection in primary care and community settings
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive hepatitis C management program including: risk-based screening, treatment initiation and monitoring, medication adherence support, side effect management, and cure verification. Collaborative care with primary care providers.
expected_outcomes: Increased hepatitis C screening rates (>90% in high-risk populations), improved treatment completion rates (>95%), high sustained virologic response rates (>95%), reduced hepatitis C transmission, decreased liver-related complications.
evidence_base: Falade-Nwulia et al. (2017). Oral direct-acting agent therapy for hepatitis C virus infection: a systematic review. Annals of Internal Medicine, 166(9), 637-648.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Osteoporosis Prevention by Clinical Pharmacists
target_population: Postmenopausal women and elderly adults at risk for osteoporotic fractures
implementation_guidance: Deliver comprehensive osteoporosis prevention program including: bone density screening coordination, calcium and vitamin D optimization, fall risk assessment, medication management, and lifestyle counseling. Quarterly assessments with annual bone density monitoring.
expected_outcomes: Improved bone mineral density, reduced fracture risk (20-40% decrease), enhanced medication adherence for osteoporosis treatments, improved calcium and vitamin D intake, reduced fall risk.
evidence_base: Gillespie et al. (2012). Interventions for preventing falls in older people living in the community. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, (9), CD007146.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Weight Management by Behavioral Health Care Managers
target_population: Adults with obesity and related comorbidities in primary care settings
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive weight management program including: behavioral counseling, goal setting, dietary modification support, physical activity planning, and psychological support. Individual and group sessions over 12 months with ongoing maintenance.
expected_outcomes: Clinically significant weight loss (5-10% of body weight), improved metabolic parameters, enhanced quality of life, reduced obesity-related comorbidities, sustained weight loss maintenance.
evidence_base: Wadden et al. (2011). Lifestyle modification for obesity: new developments in diet, physical activity, and behavior therapy. Circulation, 125(9), 1157-1170.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Sleep Disorder Management by Nurse Care Managers
target_population: Adults with sleep disorders and related health conditions in primary care settings
implementation_guidance: Deliver comprehensive sleep disorder management including: sleep hygiene education, sleep study coordination, CPAP therapy support, behavioral interventions, and comorbidity management. Monthly follow-up with sleep medicine collaboration.
expected_outcomes: Improved sleep quality scores, reduced daytime sleepiness, enhanced CPAP adherence (>80% nightly use), improved cardiovascular outcomes, better quality of life measures.
evidence_base: Qaseem et al. (2013). Diagnosis of obstructive sleep apnea in adults: a clinical practice guideline from the American College of Physicians. Annals of Internal Medicine, 161(3), 210-220.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Medication Adherence in HIV by Clinical Pharmacists
target_population: Adults with HIV infection on antiretroviral therapy
implementation_guidance: Provide comprehensive HIV medication management including: adherence counseling, side effect management, drug interaction screening, resistance testing coordination, and treatment optimization. Monthly visits with infectious disease collaboration.
expected_outcomes: Improved medication adherence (>95% doses taken), achieved viral suppression (>90% undetectable viral load), reduced HIV transmission risk, enhanced quality of life, decreased HIV-related complications.
evidence_base: Rathbun et al. (2005). Clinical pharmacist activities in HIV primary care. American Journal of Health-System Pharmacy, 62(11), 1186-1190.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Geriatric Care Coordination by Social Workers
target_population: Elderly adults with complex medical and social needs transitioning between care settings
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive geriatric care coordination including: comprehensive geriatric assessment, care plan development, family caregiver support, community resource linkage, and advance care planning. Intensive case management with interdisciplinary team approach.
expected_outcomes: Improved functional status, reduced hospitalizations and emergency department visits, enhanced caregiver satisfaction, increased use of community services, improved advance directive completion.
evidence_base: Stuck et al. (2002). Comprehensive geriatric assessment: a meta-analysis of controlled trials. Lancet, 360(9342), 1032-1038.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Palliative Care Coordination by Nurse Care Managers
target_population: Patients with serious illness and their families in healthcare and community settings
implementation_guidance: Deliver comprehensive palliative care coordination including: symptom management, goals of care discussions, advance care planning, family support, and care transitions coordination. Interdisciplinary team approach with 24/7 on-call support.
expected_outcomes: Improved quality of life scores, reduced symptom burden, enhanced patient and family satisfaction, increased advance directive completion, reduced healthcare utilization, improved end-of-life care quality.
evidence_base: Higginson et al. (2014). Is there evidence that palliative care teams alter end-of-life experiences of patients and their caregivers? Journal of Pain and Symptom Management, 48(4), 672-677.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Wound Care Management by Nurse Care Managers
target_population: Patients with chronic wounds in home and community settings
implementation_guidance: Implement evidence-based wound care management including: wound assessment and documentation, appropriate dressing selection, infection prevention, patient and caregiver education, and care coordination with wound specialists. Weekly visits with telemedicine support.
expected_outcomes: Improved wound healing rates (>80% complete healing), reduced wound-related infections, decreased time to healing, enhanced patient and caregiver knowledge, reduced healthcare costs.
evidence_base: Moore et al. (2014). Systematic review of wound care management: dressings and topical agents used in the healing process. International Wound Journal, 11(4), 375-389.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Nutrition Counseling by Community Health Workers
target_population: Adults with diet-related chronic conditions in underserved communities
implementation_guidance: Deliver comprehensive nutrition education program including: dietary assessment, meal planning, grocery shopping assistance, cooking demonstrations, and behavior change support. Group and individual sessions over 6 months with ongoing support.
expected_outcomes: Improved dietary quality scores, increased fruit and vegetable consumption, reduced sodium intake, enhanced nutrition knowledge, improved chronic disease management, weight loss where appropriate.
evidence_base: Rosal et al. (2011). A culturally adapted lifestyle intervention for Latinos with type 2 diabetes. Diabetes Educator, 37(2), 258-267.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Physical Activity Promotion by Community Health Workers
target_population: Adults with sedentary lifestyles and chronic conditions in community settings
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive physical activity promotion program including: fitness assessment, individualized exercise planning, group exercise classes, walking programs, and behavior change support. Community-based activities over 12 months.
expected_outcomes: Increased physical activity levels (>150 minutes moderate activity weekly), improved cardiovascular fitness, enhanced quality of life, reduced chronic disease risk factors, increased social support for physical activity.
evidence_base: Foster et al. (2013). The effectiveness of workplace health promotion programmes for increasing physical activity: a systematic review. Health Education Journal, 72(1), 1-22.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Health Literacy Improvement by Community Health Workers
target_population: Adults with limited health literacy in underserved communities
implementation_guidance: Deliver comprehensive health literacy improvement program including: health information simplification, teach-back method training, navigation assistance, advocacy skills development, and empowerment education. Individual and group sessions over 6 months.
expected_outcomes: Improved health literacy scores, enhanced healthcare navigation skills, increased patient activation measures, improved medication adherence, better chronic disease self-management, reduced healthcare disparities.
evidence_base: Schillinger et al. (2003). Association of health literacy with diabetes outcomes. JAMA, 289(4), 475-482.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Telehealth Coordination by Care Coordinators
target_population: Patients with chronic conditions requiring remote monitoring and care coordination
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive telehealth program including: remote monitoring setup, technology training, virtual visit coordination, data interpretation, and care plan adjustments. 24/7 monitoring with scheduled virtual visits.
expected_outcomes: Improved chronic disease management, reduced hospitalizations, enhanced patient satisfaction with care, increased healthcare access, improved medication adherence, reduced healthcare costs.
evidence_base: Bashshur et al. (2014). The taxonomy of telemedicine. Telemedicine and e-Health, 20(9), 769-800.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Medication Therapy Management by Clinical Pharmacists
target_population: Adults with multiple medications and chronic conditions in community pharmacy settings
implementation_guidance: Provide comprehensive medication therapy management including: medication review, therapy optimization, adherence assessment, cost reduction strategies, and provider communication. Quarterly comprehensive reviews with monthly follow-up.
expected_outcomes: Reduced medication-related problems, improved medication adherence, decreased adverse drug events, reduced healthcare costs, enhanced patient satisfaction with medication management.
evidence_base: Viswanathan et al. (2015). Medication therapy management interventions in outpatient settings: a systematic review and meta-analysis. JAMA Internal Medicine, 175(1), 76-87.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Cancer Survivorship Care by Nurse Care Managers
target_population: Cancer survivors transitioning from active treatment to survivorship care
implementation_guidance: Deliver comprehensive cancer survivorship care including: survivorship care plan development, late effects monitoring, psychosocial support, healthy lifestyle promotion, and care coordination. Quarterly visits with annual comprehensive assessments.
expected_outcomes: Improved quality of life scores, enhanced survivorship knowledge, reduced anxiety and depression, improved healthy behaviors, increased healthcare engagement, better long-term health outcomes.
